When the capsule hatch finally opened, the first thing the crew noticed was the smell: warm grass, salt air, and something faintly metallic from the heat shield. They had been gone for two hundred and ten days. One by one, recovery teams lifted them from the seats and set them in reclining chairs on the deck, where medical staff checked their pulses and asked them to describe how they felt. The commander smiled and said her legs felt like they belonged to someone else. Gravity, after so long, was a heavy blanket. A flight surgeon handed each of them a cup of water, and for a moment nobody spoke; they just held the cups, feeling the weight of the liquid shift against the sides. Behind them the capsule ticked as it cooled, a charred shell that had carried four people home through a wall of fire.
